tools.description:
Check an AS_PATH against the published ASPA objects (RPKI attestations of which providers a network authorises), following the verification procedure of draft-ietf-sidrops-aspa-verification. The result is valid, invalid or unknown, with the reason and the first hop that broke the path.

tools.name: check_lookalike
tools.description:
Check whether one domain or Web3 name is a visual look-alike (homograph): letters from different scripts mixed in one label, or every non-ASCII letter having a Latin twin, so раураl.com reads as paypal.com. Returns the scripts used and the Latin name it imitates.

Use it to screen candidate or incom

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_mail_security, list_data_sources, lookup_target · Private data: check_mail_security, check_route, get_tld_info, list_data_sources, lookup_target · Public sink: check_mail_security, get_tld_info, lookup_target · Destructive: lookup_many.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_mail_security, list_data_sources, lookup_target · Private data: check_mail_security, check_route, get_tld_info, list_data_sources, lookup_target · Public sink: check_mail_security, get_tld_info, lookup_target · Destructive: lookup_many

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "lookup_target" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
